purpose: Agent-authored diagnostic queries, fixed before retrieval. Expected IDs are source records, not exhaustive relevance judgments.

cases.query: A residual solvent GC run started acceptably, but the final bracket produced unusually large toluene and ether peaks, pushing overall standard variability above ten percent.
The chromatography data server stopped midway through a degradation sequence. Later injections had drifting baselines and shifted peaks, and no closing standard was available.
A shared facility monitoring system passed its calibration due date while bulk media simulations continued in an aseptic suite.
An old dissolved oxygen probe failed its post calibration check after being removed. Its service life and usage were identified as the reason, and a replacement probe was fitted.
Personnel monitoring detected a single colony on an operator's left glove in a Grade A sterile area, where the action threshold was below one colony per glove.

Prefiltration microbiology samples were delivered to the laboratory late in the day and stayed at ambient temperature overnight instead of being refrigerated at two to eight degrees. Testing still began within twenty four hours.
During the minus forty five degree freezing hold, a lyophilizer alarmed because shelf temperatures deviated. The silicone oil expansion vessel had low pressure and oil circulation was inadequate.

A logger showed refrigerated product warming to about twenty six degrees for seventeen days. The investigation established that the excursion began after dispatch from the external warehouse, beyond the manufacturing site's custody.

A tablet hardness instrument label incorrectly allowed an extra month before use was prohibited. Internal calibration should have had no grace period, so recalibration happened after seven months instead of six.
A customer received a commercial drum shipment with damaged pallets and incomplete drum labels. Required checks and entries had been left blank on the labels.
Sterilized filling needles were wet on the outside after cleaning. Water trapped in nitrogen exhaust piping interfered with cooling and drying of the dosing loop.
Après le nettoyage de la géluleuse TG08, le prélèvement du tube à poudre de principe actif dépasse la limite admissible. La pièce doit être nettoyée puis contrôlée de nouveau avant toute fabrication.
A pre use process filter printout said the bubble point could not be obtained, yet the batch record marked the test as passing. Subsequent operator checks failed to catch the discrepancy.
Annual aerosol challenge testing found excessive penetration through a wall mounted cleanroom HEPA unit: leakage was 2.4 percent against a limit of 0.01 percent.
Batch review found that analog temperature charts for four hours of depyrogenation tunnel operation and the filling machine cleaning sterilization cycle were missing from the manufacturing paperwork.
Operators documented three oven sterilization cycles for removable bottom trays, but only two cycle printouts were attached to the manufacturing record.

The source of a metal fragment in a bottle of oral suspension was traced to fine granular sucrose. The particles were inherent to the sugar refining process rather than generated by the packaging equipment.

A complaint alleged foreign particles in a prefilled injection syringe. The unit was unavailable for examination and the manufacturing investigation could not substantiate the defect, so the complaint was classified as not valid.
A five minute electrical interruption stopped an enteric coating pan. Tablets stuck together before restart and the batch was subsequently considered unsuitable for further processing.
A site electrical supply interruption lasted only two or three seconds in the early afternoon. Quality assurance opened a separate assessment for possible impact on product.

Repeated reports of cracked and leaking capsules led to a trend deviation and a corrective action feasibility study, even though release testing met specification and no manufacturing cause was established.
A consumer placed two cold and flu liquid capsules in a hand and noticed orange fluid on the skin. The bottle also appeared wet with orange liquid.

Compressed tablets were forgotten in an airlock without controlled temperature or humidity for twenty six days during a shutdown. Missing written instructions and poor shift handover communication were identified as causes.

Sticky capsule blend caused difficulties cleaning the powder feed tube. The part was washed and sampled again, no subsequent production had occurred, and manufacturing moved to a capsule machine with a different cleaning process.
Operators saw loose powder inside blister pockets during packaging. Inspection showed the two parts of the capsule shell were not fully joined, so the line was stopped.
Unexpected particles were observed in the liquid while setting the spray delivery rate on a granulator before processing the batch.
